speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have yellowing of the skin and eyes along with some agitation. Can you tell me if you have been experiencing any abdominal pain, fever, or changes in your urine or stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and new-onset jaundice, have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools, and do you have any right-sided abdominal pain or fever? I need to know if you’ve had any recent tattoos, piercings, or shared needles, as these are significant risk factors for viral hepatitis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do you have any nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite, and have you experienced any recent unexplained bruising or bleeding? I will now request specific blood tests to evaluate your liver function and check for viral hepatitis markers.

REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Hepatitis A, B, and C serology, Coagulation Profile

speaker: Doctor
text:
Your lab results show severely elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin, along with impaired clotting, which strongly suggests acute liver failure. Given your history, I need to confirm if you have any confusion, sleep disturbances, or if you've been taking any new medications or herbal supplements recently.

REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen level, Ammonia level

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since acetaminophen toxicity and hyperammonemia are ruled out, I need to clarify your recent substance use; have you consumed any mushrooms or taken any new supplements, and can you confirm if your agitation is accompanied by confusion or disorientation? I will now request the specific viral hepatitis serology results to determine the etiology of your liver failure.

REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis A, B, and C serology results

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the negative results for common viral hepatitis and toxins, I need to check for other causes of acute liver failure. Have you recently traveled internationally or consumed raw seafood, and have you experienced any joint pain or skin rash? I will now request an autoimmune hepatitis panel and a test for Hepatitis E.

REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune hepatitis panel, Hepatitis E IgM

speaker: Doctor
text:
With common viral, toxic, and autoimmune causes ruled out, I suspect an atypical viral etiology given your age and risk factors. I will now request tests for Hepatitis A IgM, Hepatitis B surface antigen and IgM core antibody, and Hepatitis E RNA to definitively identify the cause.

REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis A IgM, Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis B IgM core antibody, Hepatitis E RNA

speaker: Doctor
text: With standard viral, toxic, and autoimmune causes ruled out, I suspect a less common etiology such as HSV hepatitis or acute HIV given your high-risk sexual history. REQUEST TEST: HSV PCR, HIV Ag/Ab combo test

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative results for common viral, toxic, and autoimmune causes, I suspect a rare viral etiology like Hepatitis A or B variant, or potentially acute Budd-Chiari syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Doppler Ultrasound, Hepatitis A IgM, Hepatitis B IgM core antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the young age, high-risk sexual history, and acute liver failure with negative standard viral/toxic workup, I suspect acute HIV infection presenting with hepatitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute HIV Infection
